newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin backs draft union treaty with Belarus - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin backs draft union treaty with Belarus - Tass.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin approved on Monday a draft accord on forming a union between Russia and Belarus, a Kremlin aide told Itar-Tass news agency.

Yeltsin's top foreign affairs adviser, Dmitry Ryurikov, told Tass the Kremlin leader had given the green light to the accord, which is due to be signed in Moscow on Wednesday with Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko.

"Russian President Boris Yeltsin has on the whole approved the draft Union Treaty between Russia and Belarus," Tass said, but quoted Ryurikov as saying the draft could still be amended before it is signed.

The text of the document has not been published. But a draft obtained by Reuters on Monday provided for a union under which the two states would remain independent but coordinate their foreign, economic and military policies closely.
It said citizens of both countries would have common citizenship and that the union would be open for other independent countries.
The union would develop a joint legal system, joint running of energy, transport and communications systems, promote mutual trade and adhere to a common customs policy.
It would not immediately introduce a single currency but would prepare for such step.
Kremlin officials have said the people of Belarus and Russia will not wake up in a different country once the agreement is signed but describe it as an accord of "colossal importance".

Kremlin sources said liberals in the government had mounted a rearguard action to prevent Yeltsin signing the document, which they fear could allow the hardline Lukashenko to gain a slice of power in Russia.

Russian liberals are also concerned by the economic implications of their country of 150 million people integrating with a smaller and less wealthy state of about 10 million people where economic reforms have made less headway.
